title: Taifa of Tejada
capsule: The Taifa of Tejada was an ephemeral Muslim kingdom in southwestern al-Andalus, in what is now the province of Huelva in Andalusia, taking its name from the town of Tejada in the Niebla district. It emerged around 1145-1147 amid the collapse of Almoravid rule and the second taifa period, under Yusuf al-Khazraji of the Arab Banu Khazraj, who was based at nearby Niebla. The statelet survived only a few years before the advancing Almohad Caliphate absorbed it around 1150-1152, and it left virtually no administrative record beyond its brief dynastic attestation.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. This is among the least documented second-taifa kingdoms; territorial limits are essentially unknown beyond the capital, and even the precise regnal dates are debated in secondary sources.
